definition: Vocabulary mismatch is a common phenomenon in the usage of natural languages, occurring when different people name the same thing or concept differently.
details: It is also known as the vocabulary problem, vocabulary gap, term mismatch, or semantic gap. Furnas et al. (1987) were perhaps the first to quantitatively study the vocabulary mismatch problem. Their results show that on average 80% of the times different people (experts in the same field) will name the same thing differently. There are usually tens of possible names that can be attributed to the same thing. This research motivated the work on latent semantic indexing.

explainer.lead: Vocabulary mismatch is when different people name the same thing or concept differently, and it matters because it breaks search and retrieval that rely on matching words.

tiers.eli5: It's like two people calling the same remote control a 'clicker' and a 'zapper' — if you search for one word, you miss the other.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers counter it with synonym expansion or embedding-based retrieval rather than exact term matching; a pitfall is that pure lexical matching silently fails on reworded queries.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally it is the gap between the terms a user supplies and the terms an index uses for the same concept; Furnas et al. (1987) found people name the same thing differently about 80% of the time, with tens of possible names per thing.

explainer.example: A user searches 'laptop battery life' while the document says 'notebook runtime', and a keyword search returns nothing.
